current_workflow.step: After each operating day the real-time trader looks over what happened: CISO declines, incs and decs, cuts, misentered schedules. Each item is written up as a free-text email to settlements or the scheduling group, listing hour ending, schedule ID and book.
The trader works out the expected revenue for congestion relief and replacement reserve capacity by hand and emails the figure so settlements can check it against the CAISO statement.
The next morning the trader gets the DPR, runs a BOM SAR, spots double or wrong deal entries, zeroes them out in Enpower and emails settlements to explain the revenue impact.
Annuities between books (for example ST-CALI to ST-WHOURLY) are agreed with the desk head and passed to settlements by email to book.
When the monthly PMA arrives, the trader checks each adjustment against Enpower and the inc sheet. Where they disagree he escalates to settlements and asks for a meeting to true it up.

Position manager variances, from schedule errors or counterparties such as Enron Canada, are reported by email. Schedule corrections arrive from other desks with instructions to change load zones until the position is flat.
Disputed trades with nothing written down are settled by having a recorded-line tape pulled.

implementation_steps: Collect last year's reconciliation emails from the real-time desk and list the break types: schedule direction or firmness errors, double entry, unposted price changes, congestion and reserve revenue, annuities and PMA disputes. Agree with settlements which ones the job must catch.
Get read access to Enpower deal extracts and to CAPS final schedules. Confirm the shared keys (schedule ID, hour ending, book, counterparty) and how ECTRT and ECTSTSW schedules map to Enpower books.
Build the matching job and the duplicate-deal detector. Run them alongside the existing DPR and BOM SAR check for two to four weeks and compare their output with the breaks the desk actually reports.
Add the CAISO award loader and expected-revenue calculation. Where no data feed exists, allow a manual upload of the desk's award file.
Set up the break log with settlements (Virginia Thompson, Heather Dunton, Jim Reyes) as owners of closing items. Load the currently open PMA and price-correction items.
Add the month-end PMA checker and run it on the next PMA before the desk reviews it.
Switch the morning email on for the real-time desk and settlements. Retire the free-text adjustment emails for any break type the job reliably catches.
risks: The evidence doesn't show whether Enpower or CAPS can export data automatically or in what format. Confirm extract access before committing, or start from scheduled report exports.
Position manager itself showed false variances. The job should compare source records, not position manager totals, and treat position manager only as a cross-check.
CAISO data can be missing (their server went down). The job must mark those hours unconfirmed, not zero, so it doesn't report false breaks.
Schedule IDs and books are entered inconsistently, for example ECTRT against ECTSTSW. Matching rules need a maintained mapping table or the job will generate noise.

All evidence comes from one mailbox (williams-w3), and the calculated handling value is small (about $77 a month, $924 a year at $85/h). The case rests on catching breaks earlier rather than on hours saved. Scope it as a lightweight script first.
The evidence doesn't describe the PMA file layout. The month-end checker may need a manual import step at first.

solution.approach: Each morning, after the DPR is produced, a reconciliation job pulls the previous day's Enpower deals by book (ECTRT, ST-WBOM, ST-CALI, ST-WHOURLY and others) and the CAPS final schedules by schedule ID and hour ending. It also loads whatever CAISO congestion and replacement reserve award data the desk can export. It matches records on schedule ID, hour ending and counterparty, then flags volume or direction mismatches (for example firm import against n-firm export), duplicate deals with the same terms, deals not in CAPS, CAPS schedules not in Enpower, and award hours with no matching revenue line. The job estimates expected congestion and capacity revenue from awarded MW and clearing price, which replaces the trader's hand calculation. Every variance goes into a running break log with an owner, a status and age. The log stays open until settlements closes it, so prior-month items such as unposted PMAs and price corrections stay visible instead of getting lost in email threads. In month-end mode, PMA lines are checked against the Enpower deal history and the inc sheet, and any adjustment those sources don't support is flagged before it is accepted.
components: daily Enpower-to-CAPS matching job keyed on schedule ID, hour ending and book
duplicate-deal detector (same book, counterparty, hour and volume entered more than once)
CAISO award loader and expected-revenue calculator for congestion and replacement reserves
break log (shared table) with owner, status, age and links to the deals involved
month-end PMA checker that compares PMA lines with the Enpower deal history and the inc sheet
inputs: Enpower deal records for the prior day by book, deal number, counterparty, price, volume and hour ending
CAPS final schedules and position manager positions by schedule ID and hour ending
CAISO congestion and replacement reserve awards and prices, where an export is available
inc sheet entries for incs, decs and declines
outputs: a morning variance list by hour, book and schedule ID, emailed to the real-time desk and settlements
an expected-revenue line for each congestion or reserve award hour, for settlements to check against the CAISO statement
a running break log with owner, status and age, including open prior-month PMAs
a month-end PMA check that flags adjustments not supported by Enpower or the inc sheet
solution.trigger: Daily schedule, after the DPR is published each morning. A month-end run starts when the PMA file is received.

stall_points.description: A price correction sits in Enpower but the revenue never flows through. The break carries over from one month to the next and needs an escalation to get trued up.
stall_points.quote: The appropriate price is in Enpower, but the revenue has never appeared (Deal #590753).

stall_points.description: A PMA from January is challenged months later because settlement notes disagree with Enpower and the inc sheet. Nothing compared the two sources when the change was made.
stall_points.quote: On TransAlta deal #509285, your notes indicate that mw volumes for HE 23 and HE 24 were reduced by 95 mws each hour.

stall_points.description: The PMA tool appears to charge again when a counterparty is changed, so the desk has to check every counterparty correction by hand.
stall_points.quote: Are we being charged for each counterparty again (like EES and ST-Cali last month), if so, we need to fix this flawed tool.

stall_points.description: Nothing was recorded for a disputed deal, so working it out means pulling tapes or tracking down the trader, and the BOM PMA is still open.
stall_points.quote: We could pull tapes?  Ask the person who did the deal?  There is nothing in notebooks.

stall_points.description: Position manager reports variances that disappear in the detail view, so the desk can't rely on it and checks positions by hand.
stall_points.quote: Position manager is also not working properly, it is reporting a variance at Pacificorp system border ? and at Palo Verde.

stall_points.description: Congestion revenue can't be confirmed from CAISO data because the CAISO site went down. The desk relies on a verbal confirmation on a recorded line.
stall_points.quote: HE18-although it shows nothing from the CAISO on their site (their server went down) is the same as HE17-the CAISO specifically relayed this to me on a recorded line.

stall_points.description: Double deal entry is caught only the next morning, after the DPR and a BOM SAR, and then has to be reversed by hand.
stall_points.quote: We had some double deal-entry last night under the ST-WBOM book.

stall_points.description: The counterparty enters a schedule wrong, so CAPS and the actual energy flow disagree until the desk finds it and asks for a manual fix.
stall_points.quote: For HE 11 and HE12, Danielle at the CISO misentered our schedule.

stays_manual: Deciding the correcting entry, zero-out or PMA amount. Settlements and the desk own the P&L effect and may need to talk to the counterparty.
Agreeing annuities between books, which needs the desk head's approval.
Disputes with the CISO/CAISO or counterparties over declined bids, cuts or misentered schedules, which need calls on recorded lines.
Pulling tapes to settle disputed deals with nothing written down.
Telling a real variance apart from a position manager display fault.
success_metric: median age of open settlement breaks (PMAs, price corrections, schedule mismatches) in the break log, and the share of breaks first found by the morning job rather than by email from the desk or settlements
summary: Today the real-time desk finds settlement breaks by hand. Bill Williams compares Enpower deals, CAPS schedules, position manager, the inc sheet and CAISO congestion and reserve awards, then emails settlements (Jim Reyes, Virginia Thompson, Heather Dunton) one hour and one deal at a time. Some of these breaks, such as PMAs and price corrections, stay open for weeks. The fix is a daily job that matches Enpower against CAPS and CAISO results by hour, book and schedule ID, and sends both teams one variance list each morning. It catches breaks before the P&L is struck and replaces many one-off emails with a single tracked list.
